question: Do three newly published same-uploader, same-scanner, uniform-medium-density CC0 B&W film scans provide an independent fit-forbidden confirmation source for the retained generic grain model?

source.name: Wikimedia Commons
source.user_agent: neuro-film-u6-p4z/1.0 (bounded B&W uniform-grain research source audit)

selection.rule: all exact embedded-profile 16-bit grayscale PNG originals for the uploader's T-MAX 100 and Tri-X 400 uniform-grain scans; no appearance-based selection and no JPEG/no-profile duplicates

observed_setup.scene_description: lens covered with white paper, focus at infinity, automatic exposure, described by uploader as a uniform medium-density negative
observed_setup.processing_description: raw scan rotated horizontally in GIMP and luminance normalized approximately to CIELAB middle gray; selected PNGs are described as 16-bit grayscale with GIMP D65 Linear Grayscale ICC
epistemic_limits: one uploader and one scanner are fixed nuisance variables, not independent scanner evidence
actual exposure, physical roll, B&W developer/process batch, scanner settings and scanner transfer are unknown
the uploader normalized luminance, so absolute density and grain amplitude are not physical truth
T-MAX has one frame and Tri-X has two; neither stock has sufficient group support for stock-specific fitting
the source can test only scanner-convolved relative NPS/ACF shape and a fit-forbidden generic model

next_gate: Only after exact acquisition: prove grayscale uint16 decode and embedded-profile identity, inspect uniformity/artifacts, freeze spatial crops, and evaluate the unchanged P4T/P4X family without fitting or threshold changes.
claim_ceiling: CC0 same-scanner B&W uniform film-scan source feasibility and fit-forbidden scanner-convolved NPS/ACF confirmation only; not stock grain, process, density, scanner or product calibration
